subject.title: refactor(session): persist restart recovery coordination state

question: Should the recovery state owner land as five temporarily unused production modules before its production admission and dispatch consumers?
rationale: Repository policy favors one canonical, exercised path without temporary dead-code exemptions, while the contributor intentionally split this state boundary for reviewability; only maintainers can choose the preferred landing sequence.

options.title: Land with first consumer
options.body: Combine the state owner with the first production admission or dispatch consumer so the modules are exercised and the Knip exemptions are unnecessary.

options.title: Approve staged boundary
options.body: Allow this prerequisite to land alone with a named follow-up PR, explicit temporary exemption ownership, and removal criteria.

options.title: Pause the split series
options.body: Keep the original implementation frozen until maintainers choose a different decomposition or adoption path.

recommendation.title: Land with first consumer
recommendation.body: Combine the state owner with the first production admission or dispatch consumer so the modules are exercised and the Knip exemptions are unnecessary.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is recent work on the session persistence and accessor boundary affected by this sequencing choice.
